hero.subtitle: Tuesday morning briefing: INEC's BVAS preparations, voter-register investigations, the CBN meeting and global security and market developments.

morningSummary:
Good morning. Tuesday's Nigerian headlines focus on election readiness and accountability. INEC has selected 17,676 polling units for a nationwide BVAS mock accreditation and result-upload exercise on 28 November. Separately, the commission says 54 personnel across 10 states have been queried over alleged voter-registration irregularities; the disciplinary process is ongoing, and allegations must not be treated as findings. INEC also says more than 1.6 million confirmed invalid registrations were removed from the preliminary register.

Delta State remains tense after an attack on Ovie Omo-Agege's campaign entourage in Ughelli North left four people dead and four critically injured, according to PUNCH. A daily 6pm–6am curfew is in force. Police say they are investigating. Campaign allegations naming political officeholders have not been independently established and should not be circulated as fact.

The CBN's two-day Monetary Policy Committee meeting continues today. Analysts cited by PUNCH expect the benchmark rate to remain at 23 per cent because of pressure on the naira and foreign-exchange reserves; this is a forecast, not the CBN's decision. Nigeria's oil revenue also faces scrutiny: the Budget Office's half-year report shows gross oil receipts fell ₦1.44 trillion year-on-year despite higher crude prices, with production and fiscal constraints limiting the benefit.

Across the wider world, Ukraine says it struck a Russian corvette in Libyan waters, but eastern Libyan officials told AP the vessel was damaged rather than sunk. The United States has added 24 Nigerians to a public immigration enforcement list, bringing the reported total to 157; listing does not establish conviction or a deportation date. In Europe, November surveys show Germany's business activity expanding while France's private sector contracts. Global currency markets are watching the dollar's strength and expectations for the US Federal Reserve.

The planned Trump–Putin meeting is due today; as of this morning, it has not taken place and no agreement should be assumed. RadiantWaves will update confirmed developments as official statements and independent reporting become available.

featured.title: Bayelsa boat disaster: families await support as investigation and safety questions continue
featured.category: Nigeria / Bayelsa / Public Safety / Water Transport
featured.summary: Governor Douye Diri reported 29 deaths and more than 50 survivors receiving treatment on Sunday. President Tinubu approved ₦250 million in support for affected families; the final passenger count remains unknown.
featured.content:
The Bayelsa boat disaster remains a major public-safety concern on Monday morning. Governor Douye Diri said on Sunday that 29 people had died and more than 50 survivors were receiving treatment. Earlier, NEMA had reported 24 bodies recovered and 24 survivors rescued. These separate updates should not be added together: authorities have not published a reconciled passenger manifest or final casualty list.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima announced that President Bola Tinubu had approved ₦250 million in support for affected families during a condolence visit to Yenagoa. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy also directed the National Inland Waterways Authority to investigate the causes. Relief funding is important, but it does not replace an independent investigation or practical enforcement.

Police and government accounts have raised questions about the vessel's condition, loading arrangements, passenger records and life jackets. These matters remain subject to investigation. Authorities should publish the passenger manifest if available, a reconciled casualty list, inspection records and the steps being taken to prevent another tragedy. The photograph supplied by a RadiantWaves reader shows a crowded waterway and passenger boats; its exact date and location have not been independently verified, so it should not be presented as a confirmed image of the accident.
featured.imageNote: Reader-supplied contextual photograph may be used only with a caption stating its date and exact location are unverified; not confirmed as the accident scene.
featured.source: Channels Television and PUNCH, 22 November 2026; NEMA; Bayelsa State Government; Office of the Vice-President statement as reported
featured.whyItMatters: The tragedy raises urgent questions about safe passenger limits, life jackets, vessel inspections, passenger manifests and emergency response on inland waterways.
featured.whatHappensNext: Track the reconciled casualty figure, NIWA investigation, distribution of relief funds and enforceable safety measures.
featured.label: BAYELSA / ACCOUNTABILITY

topStories.title: INEC selects 17,676 polling units for nationwide BVAS mock test on 28 November
topStories.summary: INEC says the mock accreditation and electronic result-upload exercise will take place in two polling units in each of the country's 8,838 Registration Areas, from 8:30am to 2:30pm on Saturday.
topStories.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has selected 17,676 polling units nationwide for a mock accreditation and electronic result-upload exercise scheduled for Saturday, 28 November 2026. INEC says two polling units will be used in each of the country's 8,838 Registration Areas. The exercise is scheduled to run from 8:30am to 2:30pm.

The commission says the test is intended to assess the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), accreditation procedures and electronic result-upload processes ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC has asked political parties, stakeholders and members of the public to consult its website for the list of selected polling units.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council had previously criticised the short preparation period and called for a postponement. The mock exercise is not a general election and its success will not, by itself, prove that every device or process will work under nationwide election-day conditions. Public reporting on results, faults detected and corrective actions will be important.
topStories.imageNote: No independently verified, reusable photograph specific to this mock exercise has been added.
topStories.source: PUNCH, 24 November 2026; INEC announcement
topStories.whyItMatters: The credibility of the 2027 election depends on reliable voter accreditation, transparent result transmission and public confidence.
topStories.whatHappensNext: INEC's mock BVAS exercise is scheduled for 28 November; monitor its findings and any remedial measures.
topStories.label: INEC / BVAS TEST

topStories.title: INEC queries 54 officials over alleged voter-registration irregularities in 10 states
topStories.summary: INEC says 54 personnel have been issued queries and will face due-process investigations; the commission also says it removed more than 1.6 million confirmed invalid registrations from the preliminary register.
topStories.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission says it has issued queries to 54 personnel across 10 states over alleged irregularities in voter registration. National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna told PUNCH that the officials have an opportunity to respond before further interviews and disciplinary decisions are considered.

INEC said the process would begin with state-level committees before a panel at its headquarters reviews the findings. The commission says the alleged breaches relate to complaints about the preliminary voters' register, including suspicious profiles, multiple registrations and manipulated photographs. These are allegations under investigation; the 54 officials should not be treated as having been found guilty.

INEC also said it had deleted more than 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations from the preliminary register generated through the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration exercise. The scale of the clean-up makes transparency especially important: the commission should publish clear explanations, protect legitimate voters from wrongful removal and report the outcomes of disciplinary proceedings.
topStories.imageNote: No reusable photograph of the investigation has been verified; image omitted.
topStories.source: PUNCH, 24 November 2026; INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna
topStories.whyItMatters: An accurate register is fundamental to equal voting rights and confidence in the 2027 elections.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for responses from the queried officials, INEC's investigation findings and safeguards against wrongful deletion.
topStories.label: ELECTIONS / REGISTER

topStories.title: Delta attack: four killed, four wounded as police investigate; Ughelli North curfew continues
topStories.summary: PUNCH reports four deaths and four critically injured after gunmen attacked Ovie Omo-Agege's campaign entourage. Police say investigations are under way; allegations naming political figures remain unproven.
topStories.content:
At least four people were reported killed and four others critically injured after gunmen attacked the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege at Uduere community in Ughelli North, Delta State, on Monday. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unharmed. The Delta State Government imposed a daily curfew from 6pm to 6am across Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The campaign organisation identified two of the dead as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro. It alleged that the attack was an assassination attempt and made accusations against the local council chairman and the state governor. PUNCH reported that these allegations had not been independently established. They must not be repeated as facts.

The Delta State Police Command says it has begun investigations to establish the circumstances and identify those responsible. It has urged residents to remain calm, comply with the curfew and provide credible information. Political violence must not be answered with retaliation or unverified accusations; the priority is a transparent investigation and protection of residents and campaigners.
topStories.imageNote: PUNCH's accompanying portrait is a file photograph and not an image of the attack; no incident photograph added.
topStories.source: PUNCH, 24 November 2026; Delta State Police Command; Delta State Government
topStories.whyItMatters: The killings raise urgent concerns about political violence and the safety of candidates, supporters and residents ahead of the 2027 elections.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Follow the police investigation, curfew enforcement and any independently verified updates on victims and arrests.
topStories.label: DELTA / CURFEW

topStories.title: CBN begins monetary policy meeting as analysts expect rates to remain at 23%
topStories.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee meets on 23–24 November. Analysts cited by PUNCH expect the benchmark rate to remain at 23%, citing pressure on the naira and foreign-exchange reserves; no decision has been announced.
topStories.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria's Monetary Policy Committee is holding its 308th meeting on 23 and 24 November. Analysts surveyed by PUNCH expect the committee to retain the Monetary Policy Rate at 23 per cent, although the decision has not yet been announced.

The analysts point to renewed pressure on the naira, a decline in foreign-exchange reserves and tighter global monetary conditions. PUNCH reported that the official exchange rate was around ₦1,394 per dollar on Friday, while the parallel-market rate was reported at about ₦1,460 on Sunday. The figures are market snapshots and can change.

Annual headline inflation was reported at 14.06 per cent in October, down from 14.63 per cent in September, according to figures cited in the report. The MPC faces a difficult balance: reducing borrowing costs could support activity, but easing too soon may add pressure to the currency and inflation expectations. The committee's actual decision and its policy statement will determine the outcome.
topStories.imageNote: PUNCH's CBN building image is a file photograph; no permission for reuse was established.
topStories.source: PUNCH, 24 November 2026; Cordros Securities; Financial Markets Dealers Association
topStories.whyItMatters: Interest-rate decisions affect borrowing costs, exchange-rate pressures, inflation and investment across the Nigerian economy.
topStories.whatHappensNext: The CBN is expected to announce its MPC decision after the two-day meeting; analysts' forecasts are not the official outcome.
topStories.label: CBN / MPC WATCH

topStories.title: Nigeria's oil revenue falls ₦1.44tn in first half of 2026 despite higher crude prices
topStories.category: Nigeria / Economy / Oil and Gas / Public Finance
topStories.summary: The Budget Office says gross oil revenue fell 15.45% year-on-year to ₦7.88tn in January–June, missing the half-year target by ₦10.78tn despite higher international prices.
topStories.content:
Nigeria recorded gross oil revenue of ₦7.88 trillion in the first half of 2026, down from about ₦9.32 trillion in the same period of 2025, according to the Budget Office of the Federation's half-year budget implementation report. PUNCH's analysis puts the decline at ₦1.44 trillion, or 15.45 per cent.

The report said revenue was ₦10.78 trillion below the half-year target of ₦18.65 trillion. This occurred even though average crude prices in the second quarter were reported at $104.52 per barrel, compared with $74 a year earlier. The Budget Office attributed the shortfall to lower-than-targeted production and lifting, weak receipts, legacy production constraints and fiscal deductions under the Petroleum Industry Act.

Average production was 1.72 million barrels per day in the second quarter, below the budget benchmark of 1.84 million barrels per day. The figures highlight that higher global prices do not automatically translate into stronger public revenue when production, investment, infrastructure and collection remain constrained.
topStories.imageNote: PUNCH's crude-oil file photograph is rights-restricted; no unlicensed copy used.
topStories.source: Budget Office of the Federation, Second Quarter and Half-Year 2026 Budget Implementation Report; PUNCH, 24 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: Oil receipts remain important to federal and state finances; persistent revenue gaps can affect budgets and public services.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Monitor production, oil lifting, petroleum tax receipts and the government's response to the revenue shortfall.
topStories.label: OIL REVENUE / BUDGET

topStories.title: Four killed in attack on Omo-Agege campaign team as Delta imposes curfew
topStories.summary: Four people were reported killed and four injured in an attack on the campaign entourage of Ovie Omo-Agege in Ughelli North. Delta State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew.
topStories.content:
At least four people were killed and four others injured when gunmen attacked the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege at Uduere in Ughelli North Local Government Area, Delta State, on Monday, 23 November. Omo-Agege, who is contesting the Delta Central senatorial seat on the Nigeria Democratic Congress platform, escaped unharmed, according to his campaign organisation and multiple Nigerian media reports.

The campaign described the incident as a targeted assassination attempt and alleged that the attackers were looking for Omo-Agege. Those allegations, including claims about who may have directed or enabled the attack, have not been independently established. Ughelli North council chairman Jaro Egbo denied allegations against him, according to Channels Television. Police had not issued a full public account in the reports available at publication.

The Delta State Government imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am until further notice. Authorities are expected to investigate the killings, establish responsibility and protect residents and political campaigners. RadiantWaves Media urges supporters and residents not to retaliate or spread unverified accusations.
topStories.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: TheCable, 23 November 2026; Channels Television, 23 November 2026; Delta State Government statement
topStories.whyItMatters: The killing of campaign supporters raises serious concerns about political violence and the safety of candidates, voters and residents ahead of Nigeria's 2027 elections.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Police investigation, confirmation of casualties, enforcement of the curfew and accountability for those responsible.
topStories.label: DELTA / POLITICAL VIOLENCE

topStories.title: Ogun: emergency farm inputs to reach 4,000 flood-affected farmers
topStories.category: Nigeria / Agriculture / Flood Recovery / Food Security
topStories.summary: The National Agricultural Development Fund says 4,000 smallholder farmers affected by 2026 floods in Ogun State will receive agricultural inputs through a seven-week recovery programme.
topStories.content:
The National Agricultural Development Fund has launched an emergency intervention for 4,000 smallholder farmers in Ogun State whose crops and agricultural assets were damaged by flooding during the 2026 rainy season. The beneficiaries include 2,800 maize farmers and 1,200 rice farmers, who are expected to receive fertilisers, herbicides and pesticides.

The seven-week programme will use a digital monitoring system to track distribution and assess farm recovery, according to the fund. The intervention could help farmers restore production, but its effectiveness will depend on whether inputs reach the intended beneficiaries on time and are appropriate for the affected farms.

The programme is a targeted response rather than a full measure of the wider flood damage. Farmers will also need functioning drainage, access to extension services, affordable finance, storage and reliable routes to market to rebuild livelihoods and reduce future vulnerability.
topStories.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: Legit.ng, 23 November 2026; National Agricultural Development Fund
topStories.relatedSourceUrls: Flood recovery affects food supply, farm incomes and the resilience of rural communities.
topStories.whyItMatters: NADF says the seven-week intervention will monitor distribution and recovery among the 4,000 farmers.
topStories.whatHappensNext: OGUN / FARM RECOVERY

topStories.title: FIFA confirms 2031 Women's World Cup hosts across four countries; UK gets 2035 edition
topStories.country: United States, Mexico, Costa Rica, Jamaica and United Kingdom
topStories.summary: FIFA has appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the 2035 tournament.
topStories.content:
FIFA's Extraordinary Congress on Monday appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as hosts of the 2035 edition.

The 2031 tournament will be the first Women's World Cup to feature 48 teams and will be staged across four countries. FIFA said both hosting appointments followed bidding processes and were approved by acclamation. The UK tournament in 2035 will be the first FIFA World Cup hosted in the country since the men's competition in 1966.

The decisions give host nations several years to plan stadiums, transport, accommodation, security and tournament operations. They also create opportunities to invest in women's football, participation, coaching and facilities, although the long-term benefits will depend on delivery beyond the tournament itself.
topStories.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: FIFA official announcement, 23 November 2026; Reuters, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: The decision shapes the future of women's football and offers host countries a long-term opportunity to grow the sport.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Host associations will move into planning for venues, infrastructure, qualification and tournament delivery.
topStories.label: SPORT / WOMEN'S WORLD CUP

topStories.title: Gaza: Israeli strikes kill three, including UNRWA employee, agency says
topStories.summary: The UN agency for Palestinian refugees and local health officials reported that Israeli strikes killed three people in Gaza, including an UNRWA employee.
topStories.content:
Israeli strikes killed three people in Gaza, including an employee of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, according to UNRWA and local health officials cited by the Associated Press on Monday. The report adds to concerns about civilian safety and the risks faced by humanitarian workers operating in the territory.

The casualty information is attributed to the agency and local health officials. Details about the precise circumstances of the strikes and any military account should be assessed separately as further information emerges. Humanitarian personnel and facilities are protected under international humanitarian law, subject to the applicable legal rules and circumstances.

The deaths come amid continuing diplomatic efforts and a wider regional security crisis. Independent reporting and transparent investigations are important to establish the circumstances, protect aid workers and ensure that civilians can access essential services.
topStories.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: Associated Press, 23 November 2026; UNRWA; local health officials
topStories.whyItMatters: The safety of civilians and humanitarian workers is essential to aid delivery and any credible path towards recovery.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Further statements from UNRWA, local authorities and relevant military authorities may clarify the circumstances.
topStories.label: GAZA / HUMANITARIAN WORKERS

topStories.title: Libya's oil exports disrupted after armed groups shut two pipelines
topStories.summary: Armed groups shut two Libyan oil pipelines, disrupting flows equivalent to about a quarter of the country's oil output, according to AP reporting.
topStories.content:
Two oil pipelines in Libya were shut by armed groups, disrupting flows estimated at about a quarter of the country's national oil output, the Associated Press reported on Monday. The interruption adds to the challenges facing a country whose energy sector has repeatedly been affected by political divisions, armed pressure and disputes over control of infrastructure.

Pipeline shutdowns can reduce export volumes, interrupt production and affect government revenues. The duration and precise operational impact will depend on how quickly the facilities can safely resume operations and whether authorities can prevent further disruption.

The latest incident highlights the connection between security, political stability and energy supply in Libya. Oil infrastructure is a major source of public revenue, making transparent management and protection of facilities important for economic recovery.
topStories.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: Associated Press, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: Disruption to oil production can affect state finances, public services and global energy supply.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Monitor whether pipeline operations resume and for any official production or export-volume updates.
topStories.label: LIBYA / OIL INFRASTRUCTURE

topStories.title: Trump and European leaders coordinate positions ahead of planned meeting with Putin
topStories.country: United States, Europe, Russia and Ukraine
topStories.summary: Donald Trump spoke with European leaders, including representatives of France, Germany and Ukraine, ahead of a planned meeting with Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, 24 November.
topStories.content:
US President Donald Trump held a virtual discussion with European leaders, including leaders from France, Germany and Ukraine, as governments coordinated positions ahead of his planned meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, 24 November. The Council on Foreign Relations' 23 November briefing said the discussions focused on a common approach to ending Russia's war against Ukraine.

Trump said Russia could face severe consequences if it does not agree to end the war. He also said territorial questions should be decided by Russia and Ukraine rather than negotiated by Washington on their behalf. The diplomatic exchanges come as Russian attacks continue and Ukraine seeks stronger air-defence support.

The meeting is planned, not a concluded agreement. Any settlement would raise difficult questions about Ukraine's sovereignty, territorial integrity, security guarantees and the role of European governments. Statements ahead of the meeting should not be confused with an agreed ceasefire or peace deal.
topStories.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: Council on Foreign Relations, Daily News Brief, 23 November 2026; Reuters reporting on Ukraine
topStories.whyItMatters: The outcome could influence the war, European security and the future of Ukraine's territorial and political choices.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for official statements after the planned Trump-Putin meeting on 24 November and any response from Kyiv and European capitals.
topStories.label: DIPLOMACY / US-RUSSIA

topStories.title: Nvidia shares surge after Jensen Huang returns as CEO, lifting US technology stocks
topStories.summary: Nvidia shares rose sharply after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to the Guardian's market report; questions about governance and export controls remain.
topStories.content:
Nvidia shares closed up 31.48 per cent at $165.05 on Monday after the company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to the Guardian's live market coverage. The rally added an estimated $952 billion to Nvidia's market value and helped lift the Nasdaq by 6.5 per cent.

The market reaction followed a period of uncertainty around leadership and reports of a wider controversy involving alleged links to technology exports. US lawmakers have questioned the administration's role and called for answers about export controls. The Guardian reported that investigations and scrutiny remain ongoing, so the share-price rebound does not resolve the underlying governance or national-security questions.

The episode illustrates how heavily markets can react to leadership changes at major technology companies, particularly those central to the artificial-intelligence investment cycle. Investors will continue to assess whether demand for chips and data-centre infrastructure can justify high valuations and debt-funded spending.

topStories.whyItMatters: Nvidia is central to the global AI chip market, so its valuation and governance can influence technology shares and investor sentiment.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch company disclosures, regulatory investigations, export-control decisions and upcoming market results.

topStories.title: COP31 ends without a final climate agreement after fossil-fuel dispute
topStories.summary: The longest UN climate summit ended without agreement on its main political text after countries rejected a draft that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
topStories.content:
COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, ended without a final political agreement after negotiations ran more than 40 hours beyond the scheduled close. The central dispute was whether the outcome should explicitly address the transition away from fossil fuels.

The European Union, the United Kingdom, Panama, the Marshall Islands and other countries objected to the proposed text, saying it was too weak and failed to address fossil fuels directly. Many developing countries also criticised the absence of clear new financial commitments to help them adapt to climate impacts. Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing states resisted language calling for a transition away from oil, gas and coal, while supporting a stronger role for carbon capture.

The Turkish and Australian conference leadership did not put forward another draft after the objections. Other decisions and work programmes were adopted, but the failure to agree on the central cover decision is a major setback for consensus-based climate diplomacy. The disagreement does not cancel previous climate commitments, but it leaves contentious issues on fossil-fuel transition and climate finance unresolved ahead of the next round of talks.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: Reuters, 23 November 2026; Associated Press, 22–23 November 2026; The Guardian, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: The outcome affects global climate cooperation, energy investment and the ability of vulnerable countries to secure support for adaptation and loss-and-damage responses.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Negotiators are expected to carry unresolved issues into the next UN climate talks in Ethiopia; attention will turn to whether countries can rebuild consensus.
topStories.label: COP31 / NO AGREEMENT

topStories.title: Food inflation remains above 20% in 19 Nigerian states despite national slowdown
topStories.category: Nigeria / Economy / Cost of Living / Food Inflation
topStories.summary: BusinessDay's analysis of NBS data says annual food inflation exceeded 20% in 19 states in October, even as the national rate eased to 19.13%.
topStories.content:
Food inflation exceeded 20 per cent in 19 of Nigeria's 36 states in October 2026, according to BusinessDay's analysis of National Bureau of Statistics data. The national annual food inflation rate moderated to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent in September, but the national figure masks substantial differences between states.

Ondo recorded 31.74 per cent annual food inflation, followed by Lagos at 31.43 per cent and Imo at 29.75 per cent. Oyo was at 28.81 per cent, while Ebonyi recorded 27.96 per cent. BusinessDay reported that the 19 states represent 52.8 per cent of the federation's states.

The monthly picture was different: nationally, food prices declined by 0.75 per cent in October, but the decline was smaller than the 1.55 per cent recorded in September. Twelve of the 19 states recorded monthly food-price increases. The figures show why a national slowdown does not necessarily mean households in every state are experiencing cheaper food. Transport costs, local supply, market access and different consumption baskets also matter.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: BusinessDay analysis of National Bureau of Statistics data, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: Food prices are a direct pressure on household budgets, poverty levels and the credibility of economic recovery.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch the next NBS CPI release and state-level market prices to see whether the national moderation spreads more evenly.
topStories.label: NIGERIA / FOOD PRICES

topStories.title: Unilever Nigeria proposes transfer of foods business to McCormick subsidiary
topStories.summary: Unilever Nigeria's board has recommended transferring its foods business assets to MCK Nigeria Ltd, a subsidiary of US-based McCormick; shareholder and regulatory approvals are still required.
topStories.content:
Unilever Nigeria Plc has recommended a proposed transfer of its foods business assets to MCK Nigeria Ltd, a subsidiary of US-based McCormick & Company. The company disclosed the proposal to the Nigerian Exchange on 23 November, following the wider global agreement between Unilever Plc and McCormick announced earlier this year.

The proposed transaction is an asset transfer for cash consideration on a cash-free and debt-free basis. Unilever Nigeria said it does not amount to a sale of shares in the Nigerian company or a change in its existing shareholding structure. If completed, the company intends to concentrate on beauty, personal care and home care products, including brands such as Vaseline, Rexona, Closeup and Pepsodent.

The proposal is not yet final. It requires shareholder approval, regulatory clearances including from the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, and completion of the relevant global transaction conditions. The company said it would provide further details, including financial terms and the date of the shareholders' meeting.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: BusinessDay, 23 November 2026; Unilever Nigeria corporate disclosure to NGX
topStories.whyItMatters: The transaction could reshape a major consumer-goods company's Nigerian portfolio, jobs, local production and competition in the food market.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Shareholders and regulators must consider the proposal; the final terms and any impact on employees, suppliers and consumers remain to be disclosed.
topStories.label: BUSINESS / UNILEVER

topStories.title: Africa's manufacturing output reaches $351bn but global share remains below 2%
topStories.summary: BusinessDay reports that African manufacturing output has grown to $351 billion, but the continent still accounts for less than 2% of global manufacturing.
topStories.content:
Africa's manufacturing output has reached an estimated $351 billion, but the continent's share of global manufacturing remains below 2 per cent, according to an analysis published by BusinessDay on 23 November. The Pan-African Manufacturers Association says population growth and urbanisation are expanding demand for processed food, construction materials, household goods and transport equipment.

The analysis argues that output growth has not yet translated into the structural transformation needed to create a much larger industrial base. Constraints include infrastructure gaps, high energy and logistics costs, limited access to finance, fragmented markets and dependence on imported inputs and technology.

The African Continental Free Trade Area offers a framework for a larger integrated market, while critical-mineral investment and changing global supply chains could create opportunities. But the potential depends on reliable power, regional transport links, predictable regulation, skills, local value addition and trade rules that help manufacturers reach customers beyond their home markets.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: BusinessDay analysis, 23 November 2026; Pan-African Manufacturers Association
topStories.whyItMatters: Industrial capacity is closely linked to jobs, exports, economic resilience and Africa's ability to capture more value from its natural resources.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for practical AfCFTA implementation, infrastructure investment and policies that support regional supply chains and local processing.
topStories.label: AFRICA / INDUSTRIALISATION

topStories.title: South Africa records 581 women murdered in three months, official figures show
topStories.category: Africa / South Africa / Crime / Gender-Based Violence
topStories.summary: South African Police Service figures for July–September 2026 record 581 adult female murder victims, prompting renewed calls for action against gender-based violence.
topStories.content:
South Africa's latest police crime statistics record 581 adult female murder victims between July and September 2026. The figures were included in the South African Police Service's second-quarter crime statistics, covering the period from July to September, and have intensified public calls for stronger action against gender-based violence.

The same official table records 149 children murdered and 4,819 adult male murder victims during the quarter. The 581 figure refers specifically to adult female victims in the official classification; it should not be confused with a broader total that includes girls or other categories. Activists held a silent protest in Cape Town ahead of the annual 16 Days of Activism campaign, which runs from 25 November to 10 December.

The statistics underline the scale of lethal violence and the need for prevention, survivor support, effective investigations and accountability. Arrests and prosecutions are important, but sustained progress also depends on reducing repeat violence and ensuring victims can access protection and support before abuse escalates.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: South African Police Service, 2026/27 second-quarter crime statistics (July–September 2026); IOL, 22 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: The figures represent a major public-safety and human-rights concern and put pressure on authorities to show measurable progress against gender-based violence.
topStories.whatHappensNext: South Africa's 16 Days of Activism campaign begins on 25 November; officials and civil-society groups are expected to renew calls for prevention and accountability.
topStories.label: SOUTH AFRICA / GBV

topStories.title: European gas prices rise as cold forecast tightens winter supply concerns
topStories.category: Europe / Energy / Cost of Living / Markets
topStories.summary: European benchmark gas prices rose as much as 8.6% on Monday amid forecasts of a prolonged cold spell and storage levels below the seasonal average.
topStories.content:
European natural-gas prices rose sharply on Monday as colder weather forecasts heightened concerns about winter supply and household energy costs. The Dutch month-ahead benchmark rose as much as 8.6 per cent to about €96.08 before settling around 4 per cent higher at €92.50, according to figures reported by The Guardian.

European gas storage was reported at approximately 69 per cent full, below the seasonal norm of around 80 per cent. Reduced liquefied-natural-gas exports from Qatar amid the Middle East conflict and heavy summer demand have added to supply concerns. Forecasts suggest colder-than-normal conditions across parts of north-west Europe, potentially increasing heating demand.

The price movement does not mean every household bill rises immediately by the same percentage. Retail tariffs, hedging arrangements, government support and national energy policies affect how wholesale prices reach consumers. In the UK, the energy regulator's price cap is expected to rise from January, increasing pressure on household budgets.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: The Guardian, 23 November 2026; Bloomberg market data
topStories.whyItMatters: Energy prices affect household affordability, industrial costs and inflation across Europe as winter demand rises.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Monitor storage levels, LNG deliveries, temperatures and the next UK Ofgem price-cap announcement.
topStories.label: EUROPE / ENERGY

topStories.title: Ukraine reports at least 14 killed in Russian strike on Kyiv region apartment block
topStories.summary: Ukrainian authorities reported at least 14 deaths after a Russian strike hit an apartment block in the Kyiv region; rescue operations continued for survivors.
topStories.content:
At least 14 people were reported killed after a Russian strike hit an apartment block in the Kyiv region, according to reporting carried by The Guardian on Monday. Rescue teams continued searching the rubble, and a seven-year-old boy was among those reported rescued alive. Earlier updates had described people still trapped beneath the collapsed structure.

The casualty figure is based on the latest reported Ukrainian account and may change as rescue work and identification continue. The attack has renewed calls for protection of civilians and independent investigation of strikes affecting residential areas.

The incident is part of a wider escalation in attacks on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. Reporting on casualty figures during an active rescue operation should be treated as provisional until local authorities and independent monitors complete verification.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared matching image has been added; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
topStories.source: The Guardian, 23 November 2026; Ukrainian authorities
topStories.whyItMatters: The strike highlights the continuing civilian cost of the war and the risks faced by residents far from the front line.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Rescue and recovery work, updated casualty reports and any international investigation will clarify the full impact.
topStories.label: UKRAINE / CIVILIAN CASUALTIES

topStories.title: CBN begins two-day policy meeting as analysts expect interest rate to remain at 23%
topStories.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee meets on 23–24 November. Analysts surveyed by BusinessDay expect the CBN to hold its benchmark rate at 23%, despite inflation easing to 14.06% in October.
topStories.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria's Monetary Policy Committee begins its 308th meeting on Monday, with deliberations continuing through Tuesday, 24 November. BusinessDay reports that analysts expect the committee to retain the Monetary Policy Rate at 23%, following September's 350-basis-point cut from 26.5%.

The expectation reflects a balance between easing inflation and concerns about liquidity, election-related spending and pressure on the naira. Headline inflation fell for a fifth consecutive month to 14.06% in October, according to figures cited by BusinessDay. However, money supply rose 24% year-on-year to ₦146.60 trillion in September, raising concerns that excess liquidity could put renewed pressure on prices.

The expected hold is an analyst forecast, not a decision already taken by the CBN. The MPC is due to announce its outcome after the meeting. Households and businesses will be watching the decision for signals on borrowing costs, inflation control, exchange-rate stability and the direction of monetary policy heading into the 2027 election cycle.

topStories.source: BusinessDay, 23 November 2026; United Capital Research; Parthian Securities; Agusto & Co.
topStories.whyItMatters: The policy rate influences lending costs, savings returns, investment and inflation expectations across the Nigerian economy.
topStories.whatHappensNext: The MPC decision and its explanation are expected after the meeting concludes on Tuesday, 24 November.
topStories.label: CBN / MPC MEETING

topStories.title: Nigeria's 2026 oil licensing round: 40 blocks could attract $280m in signature bonuses
topStories.category: Nigeria / Energy / Oil and Gas / Investment
topStories.summary: BusinessDay reports that Nigeria's 2026 licensing round offers 40 oil blocks and could generate about $280 million in signature bonuses, subject to investor interest and the terms of the process.
topStories.content:
Nigeria is seeking investors for 40 oil blocks in its 2026 licensing round, with potential signature bonuses estimated at about $280 million, according to BusinessDay's Monday report. The proposed round is part of efforts to attract capital into the upstream petroleum sector and increase exploration and production.

The estimated bonus figure is a projection, not money already received by government. Actual proceeds will depend on bids, the terms of award, due diligence, financing and whether successful bidders meet their obligations. Investors will also assess security, infrastructure, fiscal terms, oil prices and the time required to bring discoveries into production.

The public-interest test is not only how much is raised upfront. Nigerians will want transparent bidding, credible technical capacity among awardees, timely development, environmental safeguards and clear disclosure of the revenues and obligations attached to each block.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared repository image has been added; image omitted rather than mismatched.
topStories.source: BusinessDay, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: Oil licensing can affect future investment, production, public revenue and the management of Nigeria's petroleum resources.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for the official bid-round documents, qualified bidders, award criteria and final signature-bonus receipts.
topStories.label: ENERGY / 40 OIL BLOCKS

topStories.title: Nigeria's food security outlook improves as 13 crops record production growth, report says
topStories.summary: BusinessDay reports that 13 crops recorded production growth, offering a more positive food-security outlook; the scale and regional distribution of gains still matter for consumers.
topStories.content:
A new agricultural outlook reported by BusinessDay says 13 crops recorded production growth, pointing to a brighter food-security picture in parts of Nigeria. The headline is encouraging, but higher production does not automatically translate into lower food prices or improved access for every household.

Farm-gate prices, transport costs, insecurity, storage losses, imports, exchange rates and the availability of inputs all influence what consumers pay. Gains may also vary by crop and region. The report's headline should therefore be read as a production indicator rather than proof that food affordability has already improved nationwide.

For a fuller assessment, government and industry data should identify which crops increased, by how much, where production rose, and whether the gains reached local markets. Farmers also need access to finance, improved seeds, fertiliser, irrigation, storage and secure routes to market.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared repository image has been added; image omitted rather than mismatched.
topStories.source: BusinessDay, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: Food production is central to inflation, household welfare and rural livelihoods; production gains need to reach consumers and farmers.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Look for crop-by-crop data, regional breakdowns, harvest estimates and evidence of changes in wholesale and retail prices.
topStories.label: FOOD SECURITY / AGRICULTURE

topStories.title: Kwara jailbreak investigation: 20 prison officers reportedly queried after escape plot probe
topStories.summary: BusinessDay reports that 20 officers have been queried after an investigation into the Kwara jailbreak uncovered an alleged escape plot said to have been developing for months.
topStories.content:
Twenty correctional officers have reportedly been queried as part of an investigation into the jailbreak in Kwara State. BusinessDay's Monday headlines say investigators uncovered what they describe as a months-long escape plot. The queries are an investigative step and do not establish that the officers are guilty of misconduct.

The authorities will need to establish how the escape was planned, whether there were security breaches or assistance from inside the facility, and whether procedures for monitoring high-risk inmates were followed. Any disciplinary or criminal responsibility should be determined through due process and supported by evidence.

The incident renews attention on prison security, staffing, intelligence gathering, infrastructure and the management of inmates facing serious sentences. A credible public account should explain what happened, identify any institutional failures and set out measures to prevent another escape.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared repository image has been added; image omitted rather than mismatched.
topStories.source: BusinessDay, 23 November 2026
topStories.whyItMatters: A prison escape raises public-safety concerns and tests the integrity of correctional-service oversight.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Follow the official investigation, any court proceedings and the Correctional Service's account of security reforms.
topStories.label: KWARA / PRISON SECURITY

topStories.title: Sudan's capital hit by drone strikes; homes and UN building damaged
topStories.summary: AFP reports that drone strikes hit residential areas and a United Nations building in Khartoum on Sunday. A Sudanese army source blamed launches from Ethiopia, a claim not independently verified.
topStories.content:
Drone strikes hit parts of Sudan's capital, Khartoum, on Sunday, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building, according to witnesses and the UN information cited by AFP in the Gulf Times. Explosions were reported around the airport and other parts of the city between approximately 2:00am and 4:30am.

A Sudanese army source alleged that the drones had been launched from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport. That allegation has not been independently verified in the report. It should not be treated as an established finding or as proof that the Ethiopian government ordered an attack.

The incident comes amid rising tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia, with both governments accusing the other of supporting armed opponents. The allegations are denied and remain contested. Any cross-border escalation could worsen an already severe humanitarian crisis, in which millions of people have been displaced and civilians face continuing danger.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared repository image has been added; image omitted rather than mismatched.
topStories.source: AFP, published in Gulf Times, 23 November 2026; witnesses; UN; Sudanese army source
topStories.whyItMatters: Attacks in the capital and reciprocal accusations risk widening regional tensions and worsening civilian suffering.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Seek independent confirmation of the strike origin and monitor statements from Sudan, Ethiopia, the UN and African Union.
topStories.label: SUDAN / DRONE STRIKES

topStories.title: Ukraine says naval drones sank Russian corvette in Libyan waters; Libya reports damage
topStories.summary: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette MERKURY in Libyan waters. Libyan officials said the vessel was heavily damaged; the claims differ and have not been independently resolved.
topStories.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette MERKURY in Libyan waters, according to the Associated Press. Libyan officials, however, described the vessel as heavily damaged. The differing accounts mean the ship's final condition should not be stated as independently confirmed.

Ukraine also said the operation destroyed a Russian helicopter and hit a cargo ship it described as carrying weapons. The AP report separately cited Libya's coast guard on a drone strike involving a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel. These claims concern different reported incidents and should not be conflated.

If confirmed, an attack on a Russian warship far from the Black Sea would underline the widening geographic reach of the conflict and the risks to maritime traffic in the Mediterranean. Independent confirmation of the vessel's status, location and damage remains important.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared repository image has been added; image omitted rather than mismatched.
topStories.source: Associated Press, 23 November 2026; statements by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Libyan officials
topStories.whyItMatters: The report points to the potential expansion of the Ukraine war's maritime dimension and risks for commercial shipping.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Look for independent imagery, statements from the Russian military and Libyan authorities, and confirmation of the vessel's status.
topStories.label: UKRAINE / MEDITERRANEAN

topStories.title: Gaza faces long-term environmental contamination, joint analysis warns
topStories.category: Middle East / Gaza / Environment / Humanitarian Crisis
topStories.summary: An Oxfam and Conflict and Environment Observatory analysis says war-related debris and contamination have spread heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos and biological hazards across Gaza.
topStories.content:
A joint analysis by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory warns that the war in Gaza has left widespread environmental contamination that could affect Palestinians for decades. The Associated Press reports that the assessment identifies heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos and biological contaminants among the hazards associated with the destruction.

Residents described worsening sanitation, accumulated rubbish and pests, with children particularly exposed to health risks. The findings underline that the consequences of war extend beyond immediate deaths and injuries: damaged water and sanitation systems, debris and hazardous materials can affect public health long after fighting subsides.

The scale of the problem will require safe debris removal, environmental testing, restoration of water and sanitation services, and sustained humanitarian access. The analysis is a warning about long-term risks; it does not mean every site has been tested or that every contaminant is present at every location.
topStories.imageNote: No verified, rights-cleared repository image has been added; image omitted rather than mismatched.
topStories.source: Associated Press, 23 November 2026; Oxfam; Conflict and Environment Observatory
topStories.whyItMatters: Environmental contamination can prolong the humanitarian emergency and create health risks for future generations.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Watch for independent environmental sampling, public-health assessments and reconstruction plans that include safe waste and debris management.
topStories.label: GAZA / ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH

topStories.title: Bayelsa boat disaster: families await support as investigation and safety questions continue
topStories.category: Nigeria / Bayelsa / Public Safety / Water Transport
topStories.summary: Governor Douye Diri reported 29 deaths and more than 50 survivors receiving treatment on Sunday. President Tinubu approved ₦250 million in support for affected families; the final passenger count remains unknown.
topStories.content:
The Bayelsa boat disaster remains a major public-safety concern on Monday morning. Governor Douye Diri said on Sunday that 29 people had died and more than 50 survivors were receiving treatment. Earlier, NEMA had reported 24 bodies recovered and 24 survivors rescued. These separate updates should not be added together: authorities have not published a reconciled passenger manifest or final casualty list.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima announced that President Bola Tinubu had approved ₦250 million in support for affected families during a condolence visit to Yenagoa. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy also directed the National Inland Waterways Authority to investigate the causes. Relief funding is important, but it does not replace an independent investigation or practical enforcement.

Police and government accounts have raised questions about the vessel's condition, loading arrangements, passenger records and life jackets. These matters remain subject to investigation. Authorities should publish the passenger manifest if available, a reconciled casualty list, inspection records and the steps being taken to prevent another tragedy. The photograph supplied by a RadiantWaves reader shows a crowded waterway and passenger boats; its exact date and location have not been independently verified, so it should not be presented as a confirmed image of the accident.
topStories.imageNote: Reader-supplied contextual photograph may be used only with a caption stating its date and exact location are unverified; not confirmed as the accident scene.
topStories.source: Channels Television and PUNCH, 22 November 2026; NEMA; Bayelsa State Government; Office of the Vice-President statement as reported
topStories.whyItMatters: The tragedy raises urgent questions about safe passenger limits, life jackets, vessel inspections, passenger manifests and emergency response on inland waterways.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Track the reconciled casualty figure, NIWA investigation, distribution of relief funds and enforceable safety measures.
topStories.label: BAYELSA / ACCOUNTABILITY

topStories.title: WHO chief urges safe evacuation as fighting disrupts Ebola response in DR Congo
topStories.category: Africa / DR Congo / Public Health / Ebola
topStories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros says fighting near a hospital in Ituri has disrupted Ebola response work and forced health workers and partners to shelter in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.
topStories.content:
The World Health Organization's Director-General, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, has called for an end to heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Al Jazeera, AFP and Reuters report that health workers and humanitarian partners sheltered in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours as fighting disrupted hospital services and the wider Ebola response.

Tedros said the situation put patients, families and health workers at grave risk. The WHO is working with partners to arrange a safe exit for the team and to protect the hospital, staff and patients. The agency reported 11,613 cases and 5,678 deaths in the DRC as of 17 November; it said sustained, high-level transmission continued overall.

The outbreak is concentrated in eastern provinces affected by prolonged insecurity. Displacement, blocked roads and attacks near health facilities make isolation, contact tracing, vaccination and treatment more difficult. The immediate priority is safe access for medical teams and patients, followed by sustained humanitarian access and protection of health facilities.
topStories.imageNote: No verified event photograph has been added; file photographs should be clearly captioned if used.
topStories.source: Al Jazeera/AFP/Reuters, 23 November 2026; WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus; WHO situation update as of 17 November
topStories.whyItMatters: Conflict is directly obstructing outbreak response and placing patients and health workers at risk.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Follow WHO evacuation efforts, access to the hospital and the next epidemiological update.
topStories.label: DR CONGO / EBOLA RESPONSE

topStories.title: Ukraine says overnight Russian attacks kill at least 12 in Kyiv region
topStories.summary: The Guardian reports at least 12 deaths across the Kyiv region, including nine in Dymer, as rescuers search for people trapped in a collapsed apartment building.
topStories.content:
Russian attacks across Ukraine's Kyiv region killed at least 12 people, according to reporting by the Guardian and Ukrainian regional authorities. In Dymer, north of Kyiv, a strike hit a five-storey apartment building, killing at least nine people. Rescuers pulled a child alive from the rubble and were searching for people who remained trapped; an earlier emergency-service update said 11 people could not be reached.

Separate attacks killed civilians in Vyshneve and Bila Tserkva, according to regional officials cited by the Guardian. The precise toll may change as rescue operations and casualty verification continue. Russia has not provided an independently verified account of the specific strikes in the reports reviewed.

The attacks underline the continuing civilian cost of the war and the vulnerability of residential areas and essential infrastructure. Casualty figures and claims about the targets should remain attributed to Ukrainian authorities until independently verified.
topStories.imageNote: No licensed repository image has been added; AFP/Getty and AP photographs require permission.
topStories.source: The Guardian, 23 November 2026; Ukrainian regional authorities; Associated Press
topStories.whyItMatters: The strikes have caused civilian deaths and left residents trapped in damaged homes.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Monitor rescue operations, updated casualty figures and independent reporting on the locations struck.
topStories.label: UKRAINE / CIVILIAN CASUALTIES

topStories.title: Indonesia confirms 24 deaths in factory fire as rescuers search for about 30 missing
topStories.summary: Reuters reports 24 deaths confirmed by a presidential labour adviser and about 30 people still missing after a fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory.
topStories.content:
Indonesia confirmed 24 deaths after a fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande, Banten province. Reuters reports that rescuers continued searching on Monday through unstable, fire-damaged structures for about 30 people still missing.

A presidential adviser on labour issues said 24 people had died and that workplace safety protocols were being assessed. Rescue officials said 29 people had been confirmed safe, five of them hospitalised. The number of people still unaccounted for differs across reports as authorities reconcile the attendance list and rescue records; recovered remains require DNA identification, and body bags are not equivalent to a verified individual death count.

The cause remains under investigation. A preliminary account suggested an air-conditioning unit may have short-circuited, but investigators have not established the cause. The factory's chief executive is expected to be questioned about safety arrangements. The incident raises questions about evacuation procedures, building safety and enforcement of workplace standards.
topStories.imageNote: Reuters event photographs are licensed; no unlicensed image has been copied.
topStories.source: Reuters, 23 November 2026; Indonesian search-and-rescue agency; presidential labour adviser; police
topStories.whyItMatters: The fire has exposed the human cost of workplace safety failures and the difficulty of identifying victims after severe structural fires.
topStories.whatHappensNext: Follow the DNA identification process, reconciled missing-person list and official investigation into the cause.
topStories.label: INDONESIA / FACTORY FIRE

topStories.title: Belgium's airports face near-total flight shutdown during nationwide strike
topStories.summary: Air traffic controller Skeyes says regular air traffic services will be suspended from 07:00 to 21:00 local time on Monday, leaving most flights cancelled.
topStories.content:
Belgium faces major aviation disruption on Monday as air traffic control staff take part in a national strike against government austerity measures. Al Jazeera, AFP and DPA report that Skeyes, the company responsible for air traffic control, said it could not guarantee regular services between 07:00 and 21:00 local time.

Only essential emergency and safety-critical flights are expected to continue. Brussels Airport said most departing and arriving flights would have to be cancelled, while Brussels-Charleroi Airport warned of a complete shutdown of regular air traffic. Unions are also planning a large demonstration in Brussels, with disruption expected to public transport, schools, government offices and refuse collection.

Passengers should check directly with their airline before travelling to the airport and follow rebooking instructions. The strike is part of wider union opposition to austerity and reform measures under discussion by Belgium's coalition government.

worldNews.title: Ukraine says it struck Russian corvette in Libya; Libyan officials say ship was damaged, not sunk
worldNews.category: World / Europe / Libya / Ukraine War / Security
worldNews.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukrainian sea drones sank the Russian corvette MERKURY near Benghazi. Two eastern Libyan officials told AP the ship was heavily damaged, not sunk; Libya's Tripoli-based government condemned the attack.
worldNews.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian naval drones struck the Russian corvette MERKURY at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya. He said the operation also destroyed a Russian Ka-27 helicopter and hit a cargo vessel said to be carrying weapons.

The account of the ship's fate is disputed. Two eastern Libyan officials, speaking anonymously to the Associated Press because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said the corvette was heavily damaged but not sunk. Libya's Tripoli-based government condemned the attack and said it would not accept being drawn into the Russia-Ukraine war.

Ukraine's security service described the vessels as legitimate military targets because it said they supported Russia's military capabilities. The incident could widen the geographic reach of the war and complicate Libya's already divided political and security environment. The ship's condition and the full consequences of the strike require independent confirmation.
worldNews.imageNote: AP's accompanying ship image is a 2023 Russian Ministry of Defence file photograph, not the 2026 strike; omitted to avoid confusion.
worldNews.source: Associated Press, 23 November 2026; statements by Ukrainian and Libyan officials
worldNews.whyItMatters: The reported strike raises questions about the expansion of the Ukraine war, Russian military activity in Libya and Libyan sovereignty.
worldNews.whatHappensNext: Watch for independent imagery, statements from the rival Libyan authorities and confirmation of the vessel's condition.
worldNews.label: UKRAINE WAR / LIBYA

worldNews.title: Dollar holds near 20-month high as markets reassess AI rally and Fed rate outlook
worldNews.category: World / Business / Finance / Foreign Exchange / Technology
worldNews.summary: Reuters reports the dollar index near 104.32, with the euro around $1.0907 and sterling around $1.3037, after Nvidia's share rally revived expectations of a possible US rate increase next month.
worldNews.content:
The US dollar hovered near a 20-month high in early Asian trading on Tuesday after a sharp rebound in technology shares, led by Nvidia, revived market expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates further. Reuters reported the dollar index at 104.32, after touching 104.53 in the previous session.

The euro traded near $1.0907, its weakest level in more than 18 months, while sterling was around $1.3037, close to a one-year low. The yen was near 159.06 per dollar. These are market levels at the time of Reuters' report and are not fixed exchange rates.

Traders were pricing in a 25-basis-point Fed increase next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool cited by Reuters. That is a market expectation, not a Federal Reserve decision. The renewed AI rally has improved risk appetite, but the market's response remains sensitive to inflation data, corporate earnings and the cost of financing data-centre investment.
worldNews.imageNote: Reuters' dollar-banknote image is a licensed illustration; no unlicensed copy used.
worldNews.source: Reuters, 24 November 2026
worldNews.whyItMatters: Dollar strength can affect import costs, emerging-market currencies, borrowing and global capital flows.
worldNews.whatHappensNext: Watch Wednesday's US PCE inflation report and central-bank commentary for evidence on the likely rate path.
worldNews.label: GLOBAL MARKETS / DOLLAR

worldNews.title: FIFA confirms 2031 Women's World Cup hosts across four countries; UK gets 2035 edition
worldNews.country: United States, Mexico, Costa Rica, Jamaica and United Kingdom
worldNews.summary: FIFA has appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the 2035 tournament.
worldNews.content:
FIFA's Extraordinary Congress on Monday appointed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as hosts of the 2035 edition.

The 2031 tournament will be the first Women's World Cup to feature 48 teams and will be staged across four countries. FIFA said both hosting appointments followed bidding processes and were approved by acclamation. The UK tournament in 2035 will be the first FIFA World Cup hosted in the country since the men's competition in 1966.

The decisions give host nations several years to plan stadiums, transport, accommodation, security and tournament operations. They also create opportunities to invest in women's football, participation, coaching and facilities, although the long-term benefits will depend on delivery beyond the tournament itself.

worldNews.source: FIFA official announcement, 23 November 2026; Reuters, 23 November 2026
worldNews.whyItMatters: The decision shapes the future of women's football and offers host countries a long-term opportunity to grow the sport.
worldNews.whatHappensNext: Host associations will move into planning for venues, infrastructure, qualification and tournament delivery.
worldNews.label: SPORT / WOMEN'S WORLD CUP

worldNews.title: Gaza: Israeli strikes kill three, including UNRWA employee, agency says
worldNews.summary: The UN agency for Palestinian refugees and local health officials reported that Israeli strikes killed three people in Gaza, including an UNRWA employee.
worldNews.content:
Israeli strikes killed three people in Gaza, including an employee of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, according to UNRWA and local health officials cited by the Associated Press on Monday. The report adds to concerns about civilian safety and the risks faced by humanitarian workers operating in the territory.

The casualty information is attributed to the agency and local health officials. Details about the precise circumstances of the strikes and any military account should be assessed separately as further information emerges. Humanitarian personnel and facilities are protected under international humanitarian law, subject to the applicable legal rules and circumstances.

The deaths come amid continuing diplomatic efforts and a wider regional security crisis. Independent reporting and transparent investigations are important to establish the circumstances, protect aid workers and ensure that civilians can access essential services.
worldNews.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
worldNews.source: Associated Press, 23 November 2026; UNRWA; local health officials
worldNews.whyItMatters: The safety of civilians and humanitarian workers is essential to aid delivery and any credible path towards recovery.
worldNews.whatHappensNext: Further statements from UNRWA, local authorities and relevant military authorities may clarify the circumstances.
worldNews.label: GAZA / HUMANITARIAN WORKERS

worldNews.title: Trump and European leaders coordinate positions ahead of planned meeting with Putin
worldNews.country: United States, Europe, Russia and Ukraine
worldNews.summary: Donald Trump spoke with European leaders, including representatives of France, Germany and Ukraine, ahead of a planned meeting with Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, 24 November.
worldNews.content:
US President Donald Trump held a virtual discussion with European leaders, including leaders from France, Germany and Ukraine, as governments coordinated positions ahead of his planned meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, 24 November. The Council on Foreign Relations' 23 November briefing said the discussions focused on a common approach to ending Russia's war against Ukraine.

Trump said Russia could face severe consequences if it does not agree to end the war. He also said territorial questions should be decided by Russia and Ukraine rather than negotiated by Washington on their behalf. The diplomatic exchanges come as Russian attacks continue and Ukraine seeks stronger air-defence support.

The meeting is planned, not a concluded agreement. Any settlement would raise difficult questions about Ukraine's sovereignty, territorial integrity, security guarantees and the role of European governments. Statements ahead of the meeting should not be confused with an agreed ceasefire or peace deal.
worldNews.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
worldNews.source: Council on Foreign Relations, Daily News Brief, 23 November 2026; Reuters reporting on Ukraine
worldNews.whyItMatters: The outcome could influence the war, European security and the future of Ukraine's territorial and political choices.
worldNews.whatHappensNext: Watch for official statements after the planned Trump-Putin meeting on 24 November and any response from Kyiv and European capitals.
worldNews.label: DIPLOMACY / US-RUSSIA

worldNews.title: Nvidia shares surge after Jensen Huang returns as CEO, lifting US technology stocks
worldNews.summary: Nvidia shares rose sharply after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to the Guardian's market report; questions about governance and export controls remain.
worldNews.content:
Nvidia shares closed up 31.48 per cent at $165.05 on Monday after the company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to the Guardian's live market coverage. The rally added an estimated $952 billion to Nvidia's market value and helped lift the Nasdaq by 6.5 per cent.

The market reaction followed a period of uncertainty around leadership and reports of a wider controversy involving alleged links to technology exports. US lawmakers have questioned the administration's role and called for answers about export controls. The Guardian reported that investigations and scrutiny remain ongoing, so the share-price rebound does not resolve the underlying governance or national-security questions.

The episode illustrates how heavily markets can react to leadership changes at major technology companies, particularly those central to the artificial-intelligence investment cycle. Investors will continue to assess whether demand for chips and data-centre infrastructure can justify high valuations and debt-funded spending.
worldNews.imageNote: No verified matching image has been added to this report; image omitted rather than risk a misleading visual.
worldNews.source: The Guardian, business live coverage, 23 November 2026
worldNews.whyItMatters: Nvidia is central to the global AI chip market, so its valuation and governance can influence technology shares and investor sentiment.
worldNews.whatHappensNext: Watch company disclosures, regulatory investigations, export-control decisions and upcoming market results.
worldNews.label: TECH / NVIDIA

worldNews.title: COP31 ends without a final climate agreement after fossil-fuel dispute
worldNews.summary: The longest UN climate summit ended without agreement on its main political text after countries rejected a draft that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
worldNews.content:
COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, ended without a final political agreement after negotiations ran more than 40 hours beyond the scheduled close. The central dispute was whether the outcome should explicitly address the transition away from fossil fuels.

The European Union, the United Kingdom, Panama, the Marshall Islands and other countries objected to the proposed text, saying it was too weak and failed to address fossil fuels directly. Many developing countries also criticised the absence of clear new financial commitments to help them adapt to climate impacts. Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing states resisted language calling for a transition away from oil, gas and coal, while supporting a stronger role for carbon capture.

The Turkish and Australian conference leadership did not put forward another draft after the objections. Other decisions and work programmes were adopted, but the failure to agree on the central cover decision is a major setback for consensus-based climate diplomacy. The disagreement does not cancel previous climate commitments, but it leaves contentious issues on fossil-fuel transition and climate finance unresolved ahead of the next round of talks.
